_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `s.mathematical.mathematical` declares 15 mutation kinds, of which 14 address a graph and a point cloud that are no longer persisted fields but composed children, and one (`change-coefficient`) edits the labelled equation AST. Semio-NATIVE, no oracle; the decision below records both the declined candidates and the thinness of the committed vectors for the 13 graph/geometry kinds.

oracles.rationale:
📊️ A QUALIFYING CARRIER ORACLE FOR EXACTLY FIVE OF THIS SUBSET'S FIFTEEN KINDS, AND THE SCOPE IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE REGISTRATION — the same shape the already-approved `csv-rfc4180-reader` registration on the `sequence` subset already established for this repository, repeated here for a different owner and a different row shape.

WHAT MAKES IT QUALIFY AT ALL: this subset's own `MathematicalIntoCsv` serializer (`…➗️mathematical/…/📊️csv/🔖️rfc4180/✳️any/🦀️.rs:22-33`) builds one real `CsvRecord` per graph node — `[id, label(quoted), x, y]` — through genuine row logic, and the second hop `stdio.csv`'s own `encode_csv` (`…🗄️stdio/…/📊️csv/🔖️rfc4180/✳️any/🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🦀️.rs:162-172`) emits real RFC 4180 text: comma-joined fields, `\n` line endings, and RFC 4180 §2 rule-6 quoting (`escape_field` quotes whenever the source marked a field quoted OR the value itself contains a comma, quote or line break, doubling embedded quotes). This is not the `print_dsl`/pack-transmute/serde-coercion/never-reads-its-input shape that disqualifies 163 other serializers in this repository — confirmed independently by this session's own `contract` run, which flags this subset's ONLY the `md` sibling as a stub (`The md serializer emits the artifact's internal DSL text, not md`) and says nothing about the csv leg.

WHAT IT DISCHARGES, and why exactly these five: `create-node`, `delete-node`, `delete-nodes`, `change-node-label` and `move-node` each touch only `id`/`label`/`x`/`y` — the four columns this row shape carries. For these the `csv` crate's reader is a genuinely independent producer of the row set: it re-derives `id,label,x,y` from bytes without consulting this repository's own `MathematicalSnapshot`/`MathematicalGraph` types, so a bug in the mutation surfaces as a row disagreement rather than as two halves of this repository agreeing with each other.

WHAT IT CANNOT DISCHARGE, STATED AS A LIMIT AND NOT AS A GAP TO BE PAPERED OVER: `change-graph-directed`, `update-graph-algorithm` and `replace-graph` touch `directed`/`algorithm`/`seed`, none of which has a column; `connect-nodes`/`disconnect-nodes` touch `edges`, which this row shape has no column for at all (one row per NODE, none per edge); `replace-points`/`insert-point`/`remove-point`/`move-point` touch a point cloud this row shape never writes; `change-coefficient` touches the `equation` AST, likewise never written. A reader cannot witness a change to something the bytes never carried, so those ten kinds carry no `oracleRequirement` this entry discharges and instead keep the `mathematical-1-mutate-uncarried` capability recorded in `noOracleDecisions` below. Registering this oracle against all fifteen would have produced ten green results that prove nothing, which is the precise failure mode Protocol v2's per-mutation requirement exists to prevent — and the exact defect the `reimplementation-registered-as-third-party` gate polices from the other direction (this oracle reads bytes; it is never asked what a mutation should produce).

MEASURED, via this subset's own probe (`🔬️probes/📜️script.ts csv-compare`, `semio-mathematical-oracle-probe` v0.1.0 wrapping `csv` 1.4.0): two rows carrying the SAME values with different but equally legal decimal formatting (`5` against `5.0`, `10` against `10.00`) compare `equal:true, maxCoordinateDeviation:0`; one relabelled row separates as `equal:false, labelsEqual:false`; one coordinate moved by exactly 0.05 separates as `equal:false, maxCoordinateDeviation:0.05000000000000071` — the gate accepts a legitimate re-encoding and names the exact defect in two different known-bad pairs.

📖️ A READER for the ONE remaining kind that is a fact about this subset's own carrier, and a precise statement of why the other nine are not.

This subset's state splits three ways. `equation` is INLINE in `MathematicalSnapshot`, so it reaches the JSON export intact and `change-coefficient` is witnessable here. The graph's NODES reach the CSV export as `id,label,x,y`, which is why the sibling csv oracle covers exactly the five node kinds. The graph's EDGES, its `directed` flag, its `algorithm` and the geometry's POINTS reach NO carrier at all: `MathematicalIntoCsv` is declared `IoFidelity::Lossy` and emits only nodes, and the JSON export carries `notation`/`results`/`computed` as `ArtifactChild` handles whose `local_owner` is `#[serde(skip)]`, so the scene behind them is never serialised.

So `connect-nodes`, `disconnect-nodes`, `change-graph-directed`, `update-graph-algorithm`, `replace-graph`, `insert-point`, `move-point`, `remove-point` and `replace-points` are blocked on EXPORT, not on oracles — the same category as `tiff::change-byte-order`. A reader cannot witness what no carrier records, and registering one against them would be a fiction.

noOracleDecisions.rationale:
PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED by the `csv-rfc4180-mathematical-1-mutate` registration, which discharges `create-node`, `delete-node`, `delete-nodes`, `change-node-label` and `move-node` through this subset's real RFC 4180 CSV export. This decision now stands only for the remaining ten kinds — `change-graph-directed`, `update-graph-algorithm`, `replace-graph`, `connect-nodes`, `disconnect-nodes`, `replace-points`, `insert-point`, `remove-point`, `move-point` and `change-coefficient` — whose written fields (`directed`/`algorithm`/`seed`, `edges`, point-cloud geometry, the `equation` AST) no exported carrier encodes; the `md` sibling remains a confirmed `print_dsl` stub (`…📝️md/🔖️commonmark/✳️any/🦀️.rs`, this session's own `contract` run: "The md serializer emits the artifact's internal DSL text, not md").

The survey this decision already carries is kept: `petgraph` and the external CAS candidates were named and declined. THAT SURVEY STANDS, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THIS DECISION NOW RESTS ON. Surveying and declining a third-party LIBRARY is a different judgement from declining a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION, and until this re-examination that is the only judgement this decision had ever made. The sentence it used to lean on — that this subset's own shape IS its specification and so not a fact an external implementation could confirm or refute — is refuted inside this repository: `mutate-puzzle-2d-1` and `mutate-puzzle-3d-1`, whose documents carry ports inside nodes and cascade on delete, took Python second implementations over this same `.dsl.semio` carrier, from the same kind of committed material, and between them they surfaced findings no single-implementation case could produce. So THIS DECISION IS A DEBT, NOT A JUDGEMENT, and it is recorded as one here rather than left reading as a verdict.

WHAT A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION HERE WOULD BE WRITTEN FROM: `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️.json` for the document's members, the rules of `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL/📓️derivation-rules.md` that this vocabulary was derived by, and the fifteen committed `(before, mutation, after, outcome)` specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/`. The nearest transferable recipe is `mutate-puzzle-2d-1`: an id-keyed node collection with a sibling edge collection and a metadata block.

WHAT BLOCKS IT TODAY, precisely. This case's committed specification vectors are NOT declared as `asset://` fixtures. Its `Examples` table carries the payloads inline, and the Rust adapter reaches the committed `(before, mutation, after, outcome)` files through `include_str!` instead. Two consequences follow: the execution plan does not pin those files' digests, so a silently edited vector changes the result rather than the plan; and a Python reference cannot read them at all, because the Python host resolves a fixture only through the plan and raises on an undeclared URI. Declaring them — the shape `mutate-program-1`, `mutate-note-1` and `mutate-block-3d-1` already use — is the one edit that unblocks this case, and it strengthens the case whether or not a reference follows. AND, SEPARATELY, `identity-round-trip` WOULD STILL BE REFUSED. This subset's committed snapshot text grammar is the repository-wide PLACEHOLDER: its whole body is `payload = OCTET+` and its header production declares `"schema" SP "stdio.json"`, which the committed artifact contradicts on its own first line. A second reader cannot parse what no document describes — the finding `mutate-iso16757-1`, `mutate-vdi3805-1`, `mutate-program-1` and `mutate-writer-1` all report against their own subsets.

WHAT IS ASSERTED IN THE MEANTIME is unchanged and is listed in `substitutes`: the committed specification vectors, replayed end to end through the platform, and the metamorphic laws the subject handler asserts in role. The ceiling on all of it is unchanged too and is worth restating: no second producer runs beside them, so a mistake shared by the handcrafted vector and the production code passes unseen.

comparisonPipelines.description: ⚖️ The operative mathematical gate. Stage order is deliberate: parse first, because nothing downstream means anything if a carrier does not parse; then the row comparison, which is the only stage this subset's carrier supports.

stages.description: An independent RFC 4180 reader accepts both CSV carriers.
Row set, ids, labels and coordinates — the operative equality. MEASURED separation: 0 for a legitimate re-encoding against 0.05 for one moved coordinate.

comparisonPipelines.description: Carrier-level equality over the inline equation tree, read through serde_json. GATING for change-coefficient.

stages.description: An independent JSON implementation accepts both files.
Equality over the equation tree — the operative equality.

comparisonProfiles.description: ⚖️ A mathematical graph compared through its CSV row projection — id/label/x/y equality via the semantic-mathematical-csv-v1 pipeline, rather than as one JSON projection under one absolute tolerance.

The INLINE equation tree — labels, node kinds and lexemes — plus the composed-child handles exactly as they serialise. The handles are projected so that a change in which child a snapshot points at is a difference, NOT to witness the scene behind them, which they do not carry.

toleranceProfiles.description: 📏️ Near-exact, because a flat node grid has no tessellation freedom at all — x/y ARE the coordinates, not a re-sampleable curve. The only legitimate freedom is DECIMAL FORMATTING (5 against 5.0), which the comparison already normalizes by parsing to f64. The floor admits IEEE-754 round-tripping of a decimal literal and nothing else.

fixtureManifests.notes: x and y are rewritten to new numeric values; the reader recovers the new coordinates as floats, not as changed strings.

A deterministic snapshot whose inline equation is 3/4·x + 2, with change-coefficient rewriting the labelled rational coefficient to 7/5 as an edit to the JSON CARRIER, read back through serde_json — never through this repository's own mutation engine. The coefficient is a Rational lexeme pair, never an f64, matching EquationNodeKind::Rational's own round-trip-exact representation. Observability is checked before the pair is written.
